chunks: As for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Bint Ilyas, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
He said: There is no harm in fumigating the shroud of the deceased, and it is recommended for the Muslim person to fumigate his clothes when he is able to.

key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the deceased — the dead person whose body is being prepared for burial
key_terms.دُخْنَةِ: fumigation with incense — passing cloth over burning incense smoke to perfume it
key_terms.كَفَنِ: burial shroud — the cloth used to wrap a Muslim's body for interment
key_terms.يَنْبَغِي: it is recommended/appropriate — a jurisprudential marker indicating a mustahabb (recommended) act

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia Islam to fumigate the burial shroud of the deceased with incense?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes two rulings: that incense-fumigation (dukhnah) of the burial shroud (kafan) is permissible ('no harm', lā ba's), and that a Muslim is recommended to fumigate his own clothing when capable. The chapter context (bāb tajmīr al-kafan) places this squarely within funerary jurisprudence on preparing the deceased.
